source: In the 48 hours after Prince’s death was reported, he accumulated over 11 million pageviews on Wikipedia.
claim: Prince's pageviews in the 48 hours after his death totaled 11,147,180.

source: It makes sense that household names like Prince and Stephen Hawking get the most traffic immediately following their death. The bigger the star (or tragedy), the more they are searched.
claim: Prince (11,147,180) and Stephen Hawking (8,384,446) had the two highest 48-hour pageview totals after death.

claim: Among the people who met the story's pageview filters, the increase in 48-hour pageviews ranged from 5,995% (Charles Manson) to 161,429% (Kate Spade); the largest increases were Kate Spade (161,429%), Chester Bennington (160,921%), Roy Halladay (122,066%), Avicii (112,358%) and Garry Shandling (104,340%).
code: p.merge(v[v.death_index.isin([0,1])].groupby('pageid',as_index=False).views_adjusted.sum().rename(columns={'views_adjusted':'views48'}), on='pageid').query('views48>=500000 and median_views_adjusted_before>=500 and timestamp_of_death>=20150731 and timestamp_of_death<=20180702').assign(increase=lambda d: d.views48/d.median_views_adjusted_before*100).sort_values('increase',ascending=False)[['name','median_views_adjusted_before','views48','increase']]

source: While Prince had the highest number of pageviews immediately after death, they returned to near-normal levels with a couple months.
claim: Prince's pageviews returned to normal 7 weeks after death.

source: At the time of publishing, Bourdain’s traffic remains steadily and significantly higher.
claim: In the 29 days after death in the data, none of Bourdain's daily pageview counts fell within two standard deviations of his pre-death median; his lowest count (21,625) stayed above the upper bound (10,242), so his traffic had not returned to normal.
code: v[(v.pageid==p.loc[p.name=='Anthony Bourdain','pageid'].iloc[0]) & (v.death_index>=2)].assign(lower=lambda d: v[(v.pageid==d.pageid.iloc[0])&(v.death_index<0)].views_adjusted.median()-2*v[(v.pageid==d.pageid.iloc[0])&(v.death_index<0)].views_adjusted.std(), upper=lambda d: v[(v.pageid==d.pageid.iloc[0])&(v.death_index<0)].views_adjusted.median()+2*v[(v.pageid==d.pageid.iloc[0])&(v.death_index<0)].views_adjusted.std(), normal=lambda d: (d.views_adjusted>=d.lower)&(d.views_adjusted<=d.upper)).agg({'death_index':'size','normal':'sum','views_adjusted':'min','upper':'max'})

source: Dolores O'Riordan has had the highest sustained increase.
claim: O'Riordan's one-week moving average of pageviews stayed furthest above her pre-death median: over the post-30-day period it averaged a proportional increase of 11.89 over that median, more than any other person.

source: Director Wes Craven—credited for Nightmare on Elm Street, Scream, and other classics—died from brain cancer in August 2015. He saw a spike in pageviews two months later on Halloween.
claim: Wes Craven's pageviews jumped from 20,411 on October 30, 2015 to 55,806 on October 31, 2015, day 62 after his death.

source: Cornell's pageviews spiked when Linkin Park frontman Chester Bennington took his life in the same way on what would have been Cornell's 53rd birthday.
claim: Chris Cornell's pageviews jumped from 7,845 on July 19, 2017 to 482,258 on July 20 and 918,324 on July 21.
